Arnold says the child is confused rather than cursed. He recommends patience, prayer and a Christian example instead of forcing belief.

Arnold tells this widow that she need not let her friends pressure her into supporting them or moving them into her home. He encourages setting boundaries.
Arnold encourages the parent to set an example, pray and be ready with sound answers when the child asks, rather than forcing agreement.
Arnold describes their bodies as transfigured or taken and connects the discussion with the mount of transfiguration. The caption renders one biblical name unclearly.
Arnold says those who died loving Christ are already with him. He asks listeners to read 1 Thessalonians 4:13–17 together instead of isolating the phrase.
Arnold directs the parent to 1 Corinthians 5:7–8 and emphasizes Christ as Passover rather than an egg hunt.
Arnold answers no and says angels resemble people in spiritual bodies. He interprets the wings in Ezekiel’s vision through his explanation of vehicles and their landing equipment.
Arnold says it is not wrong. He encourages prayer alongside practical planning, work and rebuilding after a financial setback.
Arnold points to Mark 13 and Jeremiah 24. He connects the good and bad figs with his explanation of Israel and the final generation.
Arnold describes the elect as having stood against Satan and defended God’s throne. He connects that stand with their role in resisting deception.
Arnold says God chose them because of their stand against Satan in the first earth age. He relates their prior justification to God’s intervention in their lives.
Arnold explains Shekinah as God dwelling there. He does not accept the questioner’s description of it simply as an unpleasant burning fire for sinners.
Arnold briefly answers by calling manna angels’ food. The answer is short and does not develop the subject further.
Arnold answers no. He interprets the wording in 1 Corinthians 15 through belief in Christ’s resurrection rather than a ceremony performed on behalf of deceased people.
Arnold says the spirit returns immediately to the Father and is not free to roam the earth. He refers to Ecclesiastes 12:6–7 and distinguishes the flesh body from the spiritual body.
Arnold points to Ezekiel 13 and interprets its wording as opposing a fly-away or rapture teaching. This reports his interpretation of the passage.
Arnold rejects that teaching, referring to Jeremiah 31:29. He distinguishes a person’s own relationship with God from an inherited spiritual curse.
Arnold says Cain married a woman from the peoples he interprets Genesis 1 as describing before Adam and Eve. This is his interpretation of the creation account.
Arnold rejects a rapture escape and says Christians will be present when the antichrist comes. He refers to Mark 13 for their testimony and describes Christ returning to earth.

Arnold describes Jesus as God with us and the Holy Spirit as God’s own Spirit. He refers to John 14 in explaining the relationship of Father and Son. The saved caption blocks include adjacent questions, so the linked range is approximate.

Arnold says loved ones will recognize each other in spiritual bodies and describes those bodies as young adults without aging. He refers to Ezekiel 44. The saved caption blocks include adjacent questions, so the linked range is approximate.

In this historical broadcast Arnold favors domestic oil production and nuclear power as uses for stimulus spending. These are his political and economic opinions from that broadcast, not a current assessment.
Arnold distinguishes the physical brain from the spirit, which he describes as a person’s intellect. He says that intellect returns to God and refers to Ecclesiastes 12:6–7.

Arnold interprets 1 Corinthians 15 as everyone changing into spiritual bodies at the last trumpet. He distinguishes having a spiritual body from having an immortal soul and connects victory over death with Christ.

Arnold links the fig-tree parable and Jeremiah 24 with Israel becoming a nation in 1948. He leaves the length of the generation to God. The captions render some Psalm references and numbers uncertainly; they are not corrected here.

Arnold rejects treating arthritis, chronic illness or epilepsy as demonic possession. He also offers explanations for their causes in this recording; those explanations have not been medically verified in this FAQ.
Arnold interprets Psalm 22 as foretelling the crucifixion, including the soldiers dividing clothing. He believes Jesus repeated the whole Psalm and connects its ending with “It is finished.”
Arnold says leaven symbolizes sin and connects unleavened bread with the departure from Egypt. He compares yeast spreading through dough with sin spreading through a family.

Arnold comforts the listener by saying his mother is with the Father and that they will be reunited. He also expresses gratitude for serving in the Marine Corps and discusses his opposition to communism and socialism.

Arnold points to Revelation 11 and the killing of the two witnesses. He says their deaths precede Christ’s return by three and a half days. The listener’s introductory chronology is not independently adopted as a claim.
Arnold refers to Matthew 8:22. He interprets the father as still dying and the saying as leaving the spiritually dead to attend to that responsibility while the disciple follows Christ.
Arnold corrects the listener’s identification from Elijah to Elisha and points to 2 Kings 6:17. He describes the servant’s eyes being opened to see the protecting heavenly army.
Arnold says they were in paradise and interprets 1 Peter 3–4 as Christ offering them salvation while his body was in the tomb. He also connects Ezekiel’s dry bones with spiritual teaching.
Arnold identifies the woman as a church following the antichrist while believing it is following Christ. He connects this deception with his criticism of fly-away teaching.
Arnold criticizes the NIV wording of Isaiah 14 and recommends the KJV with Strong’s Concordance for examining Hebrew, Greek and Aramaic words. This reports his translation preference and reasoning.
Arnold presents Job’s endurance as an example for believers and the elect. He emphasizes listening to God instead of accepting the friends’ accusations and says Satan failed to turn Job against God.
Arnold says spiritual bodies appear as healthy young adults regardless of a person’s age at death. He says age and disease do not apply to those bodies.

Arnold distinguishes approaching Christ during the millennium from approaching the Father afterward. He refers to Ezekiel 44 and the role of the elect as priests. Part of the listener’s wording is unclear even to the speaker.
Arnold gives his opinion that someone who makes it to heaven would be happy rather than regretful. He labels this as his own opinion.
Arnold prefers the wording born from above in John 3. He relates it to a soul coming from God and being born through a woman, contrasting that with his explanation of the fallen angels.

Arnold calls paradise God’s place and another word for heaven. He describes it as presently beyond human sight, says Christ returns in the millennium and places the Father’s earthly dwelling after judgment. He also advises prayer to the Father in Christ’s name.

Arnold applies the passage to people accepting the false Christ after rejecting the warning that the antichrist comes first. He connects it with the sixth and seventh trumpets and says ignorance does not make that worship acceptable.
Arnold says deception is already present in part through teachings he considers human traditions. He distinguishes that preparation from the great falling away when Satan appears in person.

Arnold emphasizes seven as spiritual completeness and says the actual number is whatever fulfills that completeness. He adds that there are also elected kings and queens among the nations. He does not directly establish how an individual would recognize membership.

Arnold connects British and Russian royal families with Judah in his interpretation of ancestry and migration. The caption passage contains uncertain names and historical assertions; this is an attributed account of his answer, not verified genealogy or history.

Arnold relates predestination in Ephesians 1 to his teaching about a first earth age and an earlier stand against Satan. He recommends his Three Earth Ages study and a Companion Bible appendix for that interpretation.

Arnold says election does not determine that only the elect reach heaven. He describes the elect as helping others recognize Christ and says salvation is open to whoever believes, while those outside that election exercise free will.
Arnold does not describe unrestricted visits. He says such a visit would occur if God chose someone to deliver a message.

Arnold answers the question about Jesus and God by referring to seeing the Son as seeing the Father and to Emmanuel in Isaiah 7:14. He describes the Father as beyond the dimension humans presently see.

Arnold answers yes and says salvation is open to whoever will accept it. He says a converted person becomes a child of God. This paraphrase reports his terminology without independently establishing anyone’s ancestry.

Arnold directs the listener to Ezekiel 13 and applies it to fly-away doctrine. The caption gives a verse span extending beyond the chapter, so that span remains unverified rather than being presented as a correct reference.
In this recording Arnold recommends the ministry’s children’s book God’s Natural Truth. Current availability and ordering details have not been verified.
Arnold directs the listener to Mark 13. He does not give a verse number in this short answer.
